    "5. The method of claim 4, wherein the wireless communication system is a code division multiple access system operating according to Telecommunications Industry Association standard specified as \"IS-95B.\"",
    "6. The method of claim 4, wherein the wireless communication system is a Third Generation Partnership Projects Universal Mobile Telecommunications System.",
    "7. The method of claim 1, wherein the signal-to-noise ratio is calculated as the square of the gain on the pilot channel divided by the sum of the squares of all gains on the common channels and of all gains on the traffic channels.",
    "8. A computer program embodied on a computer-readable medium for protecting calls in danger of being dropped from a cell of a wireless communication system, the cell having a pilot channel, a plurality of common channels, and a plurality of traffic channels, each of the pilot, common and traffic channels having a gain, a priority level, and a spreading rate, the computer program comprising:\nfirst software that calculates a signal-to-noise ratio based upon a forward link of each of the plurality of traffic channels within the cell;\nsecond software that determines whether the cell is in an overload condition, based upon the signal-to-noise ratio; and\nthird software that in the presence of an overload condition:\ndetermines the value of the gain associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels within the cell;\ndetermines the priority level associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels with the cell;\ndetermines the priority level associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels with the cell;\ndetermines whether each of the plurality of traffic channels associated with the highest priority is below a maximum gain level; and\nincreases the gain of each of the plurality of traffic channels if determined to be below the maximum gain level, otherwise, if no traffic channel is determined to be below the maximum gain level, reducing the gain of traffic channels with the lowest priority.",
    "9. The computer program of claim 8, wherein the wireless communication system is a code division multiple access system operating according to Telecommunications Industry Association standard specified as \"IS-95B.\"",
    "10. The computer program of claim 8, wherein the wireless communication system is a Third Generation Partnership Projects Universal Mobile Telecommunications System.",
    "11. The computer program of claim 8, wherein the third software for reducing the gain of traffic channels with the lowest priority further comprises:\nfourth software for:\n(a) sorting the plurality of traffic channels by the determined priority level;\n(b) further sorting the plurality of traffic channels by the determined gain;\n(c) reducing the gain of the plurality of traffic channels with the highest determined gain;\n(d) reducing the spreading rate of the plurality of traffic channels reduced in step (c); and\n(e) repeating steps (b) through (d) until traffic channel(s) with the highest determined priority level is (are) saved from danger of being dropped or is (are) dropped.",
    "12. The computer program of claim 11, wherein the wireless communication system is a code division multiple access system operating according to Telecommunications Industry Association standard specified as \"IS-95B.\"",
    "13. The computer program of claim 11, wherein the wireless communication system is a Third Generation Partnership Projects Universal Mobile Telecommunications System.",
    "14. An apparatus for protecting calls in danger of being dropped from a cell of a wireless communication system, the cell having a pilot channel, a plurality of common channels, and a plurality of traffic channels, each of the pilot, common and traffic channels having a gain, a priority level, and a spreading rate, the apparatus comprising:\na computer processor running control software comprising:\nfirst control software that calculates a signal-to-noise ratio based upon a forward link of each of the plurality of traffic channels within the cell;\nsecond control software that determines whether the cell is in an overload condition, based upon the signal-to-noise ratio;\nthird control software that determines the value of the gain associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels within the cell;\nfourth control software that determines the priority level associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels with the cell;\nfifth control software that determines the priority level associated with each of the plurality of traffic channels with the cell;\nsixth control software that determines whether each of the plurality of traffic channels associated with the highest priority is below a maximum gain level; and\nseventh control software that increases the gain of each of the plurality of traffic channels if determined to be below the maximum gain level, otherwise, if no traffic channel is determined to be below the maximum gain level, reducing the gain of traffic channels with the lowest priority."

F: Patent ID: US7916675
   Title: Method and system for providing interim discontinuous reception/transmission
   Abstract: A method, terminal device, network element, system and computer program product for controlling discontinuous reception or transmission at a terminal device of a communication network are disclosed. A regular discontinuous reception or transmission cycle of a regular discontinuous reception or transmission scheme is set by using a first control layer, and in addition thereto a shorter temporary discontinuous reception or transmission cycle of an interim discontinuous reception or transmission scheme can be set by using a second control layer. This arrangement provides long discontinuous reception or transmission cycles for power consumption improvements while at the same time ensuring that the network can easily and flexibly shorten these cycles for increased data throughput, if needed.

G: Patent ID: US20120209506
   Title: NAVIGATION DEVICE, PROGRAM, AND DISPLAY METHOD
   Abstract: Provided is a navigation technique for aiding a user to develop a plan for traveling around a plurality of destinations. The navigation device causes a display unit to display a first display area and a second display area. The first display area displays icon information for specifying a facility and positional information thereof. The second display area displays a time line of a predetermined period. When the user disposes a plurality of pieces of icon information on the time line, the navigation device retrieves a route for traveling around the disposed facilities in order. As to icon information of a facility at which the user cannot arrive at the time corresponding to a position where the icon information is disposed, the navigation device indicates that the icon information is inappropriate.
   Claims: [
    "1. A navigation device, comprising:\ndisplay unit;\nstorage unit adapted to store facility information for identifying a facility, location information of the facility, and icon information of the facility; and\nevent processing unit adapted to configure a display screen in a manner that causes the display unit to display a first display area for displaying the icon information and a second display area for displaying a time line of a given period, wherein the event processing unit is configured to:\nwhen a plurality of pieces of the icon information displayed in the first display area are placed on the time line displayed in the second display area, use the location information of facilities that are associated with the plurality of pieces of the icon information to search for a route for visiting the facilities in order of the placement of the facilities, and identify a required time necessary to travel through the facilities; and\nwhen one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information placed on the time line is of a facility that cannot be reached at a date/time corresponding to a point on the time line where the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information is placed, display the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information as \"incompatible\".",
    "2.     "3. A navigation device according to claim 1, wherein the second display area comprises a free area, and wherein, in processing of displaying the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information as \"incompatible\" when the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information is of a facility that cannot be reached at a date/time corresponding to a point on the time line of the second display area where the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information is placed, the event processing unit avoids displaying the icon information that is placed in the free area as \"incompatible\".",
    "4.     "5. A navigation device according to claim 1, wherein, when one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information displayed in the first display area is moved to the second display area, the event processing unit displays the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information in a reduced size.",
    "6. A navigation device according to claim 1, wherein, when one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information displayed in the first display area is moved to the second display area, the event processing unit displays the time line of the second display area in an enlarged size.",

    "8. A navigation device according to claim 1, further comprising communication unit adapted to transmit and receives information to and from an external device, wherein, when displaying in the first display area the icon information that is associated with a facility received from the facility designation receiving unit, the event processing unit obtains the icon information from the external device via the communication unit.",
    "9. A program for a navigation device, the navigation device comprising:\ncontrol unit;\ndisplay unit; and\nstorage unit adapted to store facility information for identifying a facility, location information of the facility, and icon information of the facility, the program causing the control unit to execute:\na screen configuring step of configuring a display screen in a manner that causes the display unit to display a first display area for displaying the icon information and a second display area for displaying a time line of a given period;\na required time identifying step of, when a plurality of pieces of the icon information displayed in the first display area are placed on the time line displayed in the second display area, using the location information of facilities that are associated with the plurality of pieces of the icon information to search for a route for visiting the facilities in order of the placement of the facilities, and identifying a required time necessary to travel through the facilities; and\na compatibility displaying step of, when one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information placed on the time line is of a facility that cannot be reached at a date/time corresponding to a point on the time line where the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information is placed, displaying the one of the plurality of pieces of the icon information as \"incompatible\".",

    "14. A navigation device according to claim 11, wherein the another passing point that the editing unit uses as a replacement for the passing point to be visited next is a facility belonging to the same genre as a genre of the replaced passing point.",
    "15. A navigation device according to claim 11, wherein, when the predicted arrival time is earlier by a given amount or more, the editing unit adds a passing point to be visited before the passing point that comes up next in the information of the time line.",

H: Patent ID: US20130073789
   Title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR CONFIGURING NON-VOLATILE MEMORY
   Abstract: Systems and methods are disclosed for configuring a non-volatile memory ("NVM"). In some embodiments, each block of the NVM can include a block table-of-contents ("TOC"), which can be encoded (e.g., run-length encoded) and dynamically-sized. Thus, as user data is being programmed to a block, the size of a block TOC can be concurrently recalculated and increased only if necessary. In some embodiments, the NVM interface can use a weave sequence stored in the context information and at least one weave sequence associated with each page of a block to determine whether to replay across the pages of the block after system boot-up.

    "2. The method of claim 1, wherein the rate at which the block TOC increases in size is dependent on the at least one characteristic of the at least one write command.",
    "3. The method of claim 1, further comprising decreasing the total size of the data pages of the block.",
    "4. The method of claim 1, further comprising dynamically increasing the size of the block TOC by one page.",

    "6. The method of claim 1, wherein the default size is one page.",
    "7. The method of claim 1, wherein the block TOC is run-length encoded.",
    "8. The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one characteristic comprises at least one of the size of the at least one write command, the order of logical addresses associated with the at least one write command, and the compressibility of the user data.",
    "9. A system comprising:\na non-volatile memory (\"NVM\") comprising a plurality of blocks, wherein each block comprises a block table-of-contents (\"TOC\") and a plurality of data pages;\na bus controller operative to communicate with the NVM; and\ncontrol circuitry operative to:\nreceive at least one write command;\ndetermine whether an end boundary of a plurality of data pages of a block is within a pre-determined number of pages from a start boundary of a block TOC of the block;\nin response to determining that the end boundary of the plurality of data pages is within the pre-determined number of pages from the start boundary of the block TOC, determine that the block is full; and\nselect a new block for programming user data associated with the at least one write command.",
    "10. The system of claim 9, wherein the control circuitry is further operative to program the size of the block TOC to a last page of the block TOC.",
    "11. The system of claim 9, wherein the control circuitry is further operative to program a start weave sequence and end weave sequence to the block TOC.",
    "12. The system of claim 11, wherein the control circuitry is further operative to program the start weave sequence to a first page of the block TOC.",
    "13. The system of claim 11, wherein the control circuitry is further operative to program the end weave sequence to a last page of the block TOC.",
    "14. The system of claim 11, wherein the start weave sequence is associated with when user data was first programmed to the block.",
    "15. The system of claim 11, wherein the end weave sequence is associated with when user data was last programmed to the block.",
    "16. The system of claim 9, wherein the control circuitry is further operative to program at least one of a page type and version to the block TOC.",
    "17. The system of claim 9, wherein in response to determining that the end boundary of the plurality of data pages is not within the pre-determined number of pages from the start boundary of the block TOC, the control circuitry is operative to continue programming user data associated with the at least one write command to the block.",

**Claim 6 Analysis:** Claim 6 is not a complete claim on the supplied text; it appears to depend on another claim. Its principal subject matter is dynamic assignment of a CSCF in an IMS environment and routing service requests through that assigned CSCF. The options are evaluated for relevance to that networking context, not merely for generic assignment, routing, or computer-readable-medium language.

- **A:** Unrelated information-retrieval technology. It classifies query occurrences as relevant or non-relevant based on contextual terms. It discloses neither telecommunications service routing nor dynamic CSCF assignment.
- **B:** Relevant. It concerns subscriber mobility between telecommunications networks, service requests, service-detail records, and operation of a call/session control function server, home subscriber server, and access network to provide the service. This is pertinent to the broader dynamic selection and use of an IMS-related control function in serving a subscriber across network domains. It does not expressly disclose the narrower claimed mechanism of discovering and assigning a second-domain CSCF in response to a device normally associated with a first domain, so its relevance is to the mobility/session-control architecture rather than a verbatim anticipation of every limitation.
- **C:** Close topical negative. It expressly discloses a serving network element, including a S-CSCF, receiving SIP communication from user equipment and assigning a random string to a private subscriber identity. That is authentication/session-identification art, not assignment of a second-domain CSCF to handle a device’s service requests. It also lacks the claimed roaming/profile-based dynamic routing combination.
- **D:** Unrelated automated financial trading and quotation filtering. Networked workstations and message routing do not supply the claimed IMS/CSCF functionality.
- **E:** Unrelated peer-to-peer distributed task execution. Assignment of computational tasks to peer nodes is not assignment of a telecommunications CSCF, and no IMS roaming or domain-specific service routing is disclosed.
- **F:** Unrelated collaborative knowledge-management architecture. Its session manager and remote server do not disclose call/session control or dynamic CSCF selection.
- **G:** Unrelated stem-cell collection and bioreactor technology, with no pertinent networking disclosure.
- **H:** Concerns rule-based VPN redirection of resource-access requests. Although it selects between local handling and VPN routing, it does not disclose IMS service requests, a CSCF, domain roaming, or assignment of a second-domain call session control function. Its routing resemblance is therefore only generic.

Thus, B is the only option with substantive relevance to the claimed telecommunications mobility and call/session-control subject matter; C and H merely resemble isolated terminology without disclosing the claimed combination.

B: Patent ID: US20070072605
   Title: Seamless mobility management with service detail records
   Abstract: A method for enhancing mobility of a subscriber in a telecommunications environment. The method includes deploying with a first network operator a service that is accessible by a subscriber via a first network. The method continues with creating a service detail record containing information related to an identity of the service, e.g., defining the service. The method then involves publishing the service detail record in a service registry that is accessible by a second network operator operating a second network. The second network operator receives over the second network a request from the subscriber for the service and in response, processes the service detail record and based on such processing provides the service to the subscriber via the second network. To provide the services, the service is executed on the first network using resources of the first network allocated to the service, such as by the service detail record.

    "2. The method of claim 1, with the second network operator, receiving over the second network a request from the subscriber for the service and in response, processing the service detail record and based on the processing, providing the service to the subscriber via the second network.",

   Title: Automated trading system
   Abstract: A computerised trading system for the trading of financial instruments or commodities which enables anonymous presentation of quotes on a workstation while still allowing the workstation to filter available quotes for display, on the basis of the nature of the originating party. A central server or network connects a plurality of workstations, each associated with a respective trading floor or institution. For each trading floor or institution, generalized institution status indicators are used to provide display filtration criteria, each indicator indicating a non-specific attribute of the respective institution.

E: Patent ID: US20040098447
   Title: System and method for submitting and performing computational tasks in a distributed heterogeneous networked environment
   Abstract: System and method for submitting and performing computational tasks in a distributed heterogeneous networked environment. Embodiments may allow tasks to be submitted and run in parallel on a network of heterogeneous computers implementing a variety of operating environments. In one embodiment, a user on an originating node may advertise code on the network. Peer nodes that respond to the advertisement may receive the code. A job to be executed by the code may be split into separate tasks to distributed to the peer nodes that received the code. These tasks may be advertised on the network. Tasks may be assigned to peer nodes that respond to the task advertisements. The peer nodes may then work on the assigned tasks. Once a peer node's work on a task is completed, the peer node may return the results of the task to the originating node.

F: Patent ID: US20030009536
   Title: Method and system for collaborative knowledge management
   Abstract: A collaborative knowledge management system (CKMS) includes application interfaces collecting data objects from and providing data objects to respective application programs including, for example, word processing, spreadsheet, graphics, e-mail, general ledger, ERP and other programs and utilities. The data objects are associated with respective relationships identifying other data objects, applications and users (whereby users include, but are not limited to people, machines and software). A set of rules defines how the data objects are to react to various systems states and actions of the objects of the relationships. Objects may be stored in a common format, or lingua franca, so that diverse applications and users may form, share and interrelate knowledge provided by the data objects and collaborate in the creation of new data objects and define new relationships.
   Claims: [
    "1. A collaboration and knowledge management system comprising:\nan application interface configured to identify a data object selected by an application program;\na session manager configured to receive and buffer said data object;\na server connected to said session manager and configured to define a set of relationships associated with said data object and associate said relationships with a set of rules defining corresponding user privileges associated with said data object;\na first database configured to store and retrieve said object and said set of relationships, said first database including a plurality of data stores including (i) a Data Units database storing basic unformatted content elements, (ii) a relationship database storing said set of relationships associated with one of said unformatted content elements, and (iii) a Profile Database storing usage history and associated metadata of said data; and\na client workstation executing said application program, said application interface and a remote server platform providing said server.",

    "5. The collaboration and knowledge management system according to claim 1 wherein said application interface, session manager, API server and Database collectively include a plurality of networked hardware configurations.",
    "6. The collaboration and knowledge management system according to claim 1 wherein said application interface, session manager, API server and Database collectively include a plurality of local hardware configurations.",
    "7. A collaboration and knowledge management system comprising:\nan application interface configured to identify a data object selected by an application program;\na session manager configured to receive and buffer said data object;\na server connected to said session manager and configured to define a set of relationships associated with said data object and associate said relationships with a set of rules defining corresponding user privileges associated with said data object;\na first database configured to store and retrieve said object and said set of relationships, said first database including format conversion logic configured to reformat said data object between an application specific format and a predetermined markup language format; and\na client workstation executing said application program, said application interface and a remote server platform providing said server.",
    "8.     "9.    Title: Method of collecting placental stem cells
   Abstract: A method of collecting embryonic-like stem cells from a placenta which has been treated to remove residual cord blood by perfusing the drained placenta with an anticoagulant solution to flush out residual cells, collecting the residual cells and perfusion liquid from the drained placenta, and separating the embryonic-like cells from the residual cells and perfusion liquid. Exogenous cells can be propagated in the placental bioreactor and bioactive molecules collected therefrom.

H: Patent ID: US20060143703
   Title: Rule-based routing to resources through a network
   Abstract: Techniques for determining which resource access requests are handled locally at a remote computer, and which resource access requests are routed or "redirected" through a virtual private network. One or more routing or "redirection" rules are downloaded from a redirection rule server to a remote computer. When the node of the virtual private network running on the remote computer receives a resource access request, it compares the identified resource with the rules. Based upon how the identified resource matches one or more rules, the node will determine whether the resource access request is redirected through the virtual private network or handled locally (e.g., retrieved locally from another network). A single set of redirection rules can be distributed to and employed by a variety of different virtual private network communication techniques.
   Claims: [
